title: Runtime memory mesh stabilizer and KV shadow heal for multi-tenant GPU OOMs
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Multiple enterprise customers (hosted + dedicated) reported recurring GPU OOMs during high-concurrency workloads with non-uniform prompt prefixes. Investigation points to a subtle interaction between the allocation arena mesh and ephemeral KV shadow entries created by async eviction: tombstoned KV handles were leaving small, interleaved free regions in the GPU arena that prevented effective coalescing. Over time this 'memory mesh' fragments and causes allocations to fail even though aggregate free memory remains. The bug manifests more in Dedicated pools with higher tenant churn and in Private deployments with aggressive prefetchers.

Root cause hypothesis: async KV eviction creates short-lived shadow entries that race with arena free operations and the arena coalescer misses adjacent small holes due to epoch skew. The allocator ends up with many small non-contiguous free spans (mesh) that fail large contiguous allocation requests (for KV caches and large attention tensors), leading to OOMs.

Goal: implement a low-risk runtime patch ("memory mesh stabilizer") that performs two coordinated actions: 1) introduce an idempotent KV shadow reconciliation pass that compacts tombstones within short windows to avoid creating long-lived holes; 2) augment the arena coalescer to perform a lightweight deferred coalescing sweep on allocation hot paths and expose a feature-flagged backpressure gate to throttle prefetch/batching when mesh entropy exceeds threshold.
steps_to_reproduce: Run the customer workload (trace attached) in staging on a 4xA100 dedicated node with tenant churn enabled
Replay recorded traces with concurrent batching (batch sizes 12-48) and random prefix lengths (200-1200 tokens)
Trigger async eviction by filling KV cache then issuing interleaved short-lived sessions to force tombstone creation
acceptance_criteria: Reproduced failure mode in staging is eliminated when patch is applied: OOM count drops to zero in a 24h stress run
Memory fragmentation metric (free_span_contiguity_ratio) improves by >= 60% during stress compared to baseline
No regression in p50/p95 latency beyond 8% for high-concurrency workloads in canary tests
Patch is gated behind runtime.feature.flags.memory_mesh_stabilizer and runtime.feature.flags.kv_shadow_reconcile
Hotfix PR has tests, benchmarks, and integration test that simulates asynchronous eviction races
timeline_and_updates: 2026-02-20 - Triage: customer A (hosted) and customer B (dedicated) opened escalations. Assigned to on-call. Initial triage indicates fragmentation rather than leak.
2026-02-22 - Trace capture: full kernel traces and allocator histograms captured from both customers and replicated in staging (trace ids: trace://staging/mesh-20260222)
2026-02-25 - Spike: reproduced mesh fragmentation locally using synthetic evicter and short-lived sessions. Verified small non-contiguous free spans block large allocation requests.
2026-02-27 - Design: agreed on two-phase approach — KV shadow reconciliation + deferred coalescer sweep. Decided to feature-flag and rollout to canary pool first.
2026-03-02 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/13789 implements reconciliation pass + coalescer heuristic. Added metrics and feature flags.
2026-03-04 - Internal review: security reviewed PR surface (no new TLS endpoints). Perf reviewed: microbenchmarks show 1.6% p50 latency uplift when reconciliation enabled; acceptable for canary.
2026-03-06 - Canary deploy: enabled memory_mesh_stabilizer on 5% of dedicated pool with synthetic load. Observed immediate drop in free_span_histogram tail and 0 OOMs during 48h run.
2026-03-08 - Customer validation: invited customer B to test canary; customer reported that OOMs stopped under their workload. Going to expand canary and prepare hosted rollout.
2026-03-10 - Preparing release notes and runbook. This ticket moved to In Progress for final QA and rollout planning.
testing_plan: Unit tests for reconciliation pass (simulate tombstone races and idempotency)
Integration test: staged replica with KV eviction enabled and tenant churn harness
Performance benchmarks: rerun model serving perf with and without flags across seqlen 256..2048
Chaos test: random eviction delays and forced preemption to validate no regressions
Long-run canary: 7-day dedicated pool canary before hosted-wide rollout
rollout_and_mitigation: Canary: enable on 5% dedicated, monitor OOMs, free_span_contiguity_ratio, latency
Step-up: 25% -> 50% -> 100% for Dedicated, each step requires green on OOMs and <8% latency regression
Hosted: staged rollout behind feature flag and tenant-aware routing for first 48h
Rollback: disable feature flag and trigger allocator passive compaction job, escalate to on-call allocator lead
Mitigation if regressions: enable temporary preemptive eviction throttle (runtime.prefetch.max_inflight=2) and contact customers for manual failover
postmortem_tasks: Add allocator invariants in unit test suite to prevent regression
Instrument additional metrics: free_span_age_percentile and kv_shadow_gc_latency
Add runbook section for memory-mesh incidents and playbook for quick canary creation
Schedule follow-up: consider long-term redesign of async eviction to avoid tombstone creation under high churn
